original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Does the next simple root, in the #7017 pinned order, that moves a punctured line induce the same weight-16 set equality on its own rebuilt 112-line list?
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a measured speedup. The revision-8 verification row says a published faster replay is not equivalent coverage until checked. Open PR #7017 recorded the first moving pair and asked whether the next simple root preserves the transported weight-16 equality. This package answers that question for the next root only. It does not time an engine or rerun the first reflection.
bottleneck_link: Frame-code coverage checks remain usable only when the low-weight set still matches after the root list changes. This comparison binds the seven recorded supports to the next reflected P112 frame. It does not change a supplier bill or the selected kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after the next simple root that moves a punctured line, one rebuilt 112-line list, and one half-split compared with the transported supports. Do not half-split a later simple root, rerun the first reflection, or call the bit-lane or intersection-counter engines.
evidence: The 8 by 8 scan moves 16 pairs, on simple roots 0, 3, 5 and 7. Roots 1, 2, 4 and 6 fix every punctured line. The next simple root after the #7017 root is alpha=(0,-2,2,0,0,0,0,0), and its first moved punctured line is (2,2,0,0,0,0,0,0), sent to (2,0,2,0,0,0,0,0). The image frame moves four lines and is a different orthogonal 8-frame. The rebuilt 112-line complement has SHA256 36e3ad43dbfd53d71b20cfac522fbf9c0c1c065054994b9c81767a228d7e6f3c. Transporting the seven recorded supports gives SHA256 0ab33f7ea89182ea1cbc5ca06d5f3bdcaeb72a08aef3eaceb33e6a43bbb96636. The incidence matrix has 1260 rows, rank 76 and kernel dimension 36, with free coordinates distinct from the #7017 basis. One half-split after 18 generators visits all 68719476736 kernel words and returns exactly those seven weight-16 supports. The weight distribution equals the distribution recorded for the unreflected frame. The seven untransported integers fail frame parity. Selected kappa stays 781451/250000000.

open_questions.question: Does simple root 5, the next root after this one in the same pinned order that moves a punctured line, induce the same set equality on its own rebuilt list?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This census is simple root 3 only. The 64-pair scan records simple roots 5 and 7 as later moving roots, and a different root produces a different frame, so these transported integers do not answer them.
open_questions.first_step: Rebuild the simple-root-5 112-line complement and compare one half-split with that root's transported supports.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package stops once simple root 3 has been compared.

open_questions.question: Does low_weight_words on this simple-root-3 36-generator basis return the same seven transported supports?

This basis and hash 0ab33f7ea89182ea1cbc5ca06d5f3bdcaeb72a08aef3eaceb33e6a43bbb96636 are not the #7017 basis or hash 9ce7e5edc72ee3104d62cb068146b73840e9a3c42c4132403dece70c8146cccb.
